set.description:
A mezcal producer from San Luis Potosí came to us with a brand called Xantolo and asked for a complete renewal. The product was good. The brand looked childish and cheap, dressed in the Day of the Dead the way a movie would dress it. He wanted something that could compete in a demanding market with a daring presence, and keep the elegance of how mezcal is made.

The first decision was the name. Anything tied to the Day of the Dead or a national holiday would keep the brand inside the costume. The verbal identity had to carry courage, daring and pride, so the name became Alma Brava, brave soul: the part of you that fights for what it wants without fear of the limits along the way.

The identity is black, almost nothing else, with a typeface of generous proportions and a seal. It is elegant and fine, so the daring lives in the name and the restraint lives in the object. The brand book carries the line that sums it up: "Sentimiento icónico, orgullo de nuestra tierra."

The naming and the verbal identity. A logotype, a monogram and a seal. The brand book. The front and back label and the art direction for the bottle, and a product photoshoot. We made it at MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, between 2020 and 2021, with José Pablo as art director and Andrés Domínguez as creative director.

The Dieline and Packaging of the World both selected the work in 2021. The name was registered as a trademark the following year.

set.description:
Ando is a berry-flavored gummy made to prevent and ease alcohol flush, also known as Asian flush. The company is in Brooklyn. Its founders, Peter Czepiga and Ray Margono, met as college freshmen. Ray is Indonesian and had lived with the flush his whole adult life. In 2023, before their first production run, they came to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, for a brand that made health feel joyful.

The name was still being tested when we started, and in production the gummy itself turned a dark red, between raspberry and red wine. We chose to keep the brand free of the product's color. José Pablo put it to the founders directly: "I don't believe that the brand must be aligned to the gummy color." Crimson stayed in the palette as an accent beside cobalt and mint.

The wordmark is heavy and rounded, black on cream. The pouch explains the product in plain steps, starting with taking Ando before you drink, and leads with a promise you can say out loud: less flush, more fun. Billboards and ads carry the same voice, built around the joy of going out without the flush.

Visual identity, color, the packaging dieline, home and product page designs in Figma, and a brand book. In 2024, revised labels and a travel tin, which Peter briefed as "Fun/playful/joyful, like everything that comes from our brand."

On the home page design, Peter wrote: "Ray and I LOVE this design! I think your team did an amazing job." Ando is on sale today at andogummy.com, and new clients have come to Atla since after seeing the project.

set.description:
Fernando Ramirez started Angeles after a long stretch of stomach pain no doctor could explain. Herbal cleansing protocols worked where the visits had not. The brand grew fast, burned him out, and lost its customers when he renamed it away from an extreme niche. He came to Atla with a large audience that no longer answered, and one ask: "It isn't performing well. I know it could be doing way better."

The product is a complete herbal system in phases, clear and then nourish, priced above the shelf. The problem was translation. The site had to teach what the products do so that anyone could follow it. Fernando's words: "Dumb it down." It also had to avoid looking cheap or pushy. Buyers of wellness, the strategy found, are tired of being sold to and tired of fake wellness.

The character we gave the brand is a health strategist: confident, direct and calm, a man who has seen both sides. The line that carried was your body isn't broken, it's blocked. Fernando picked the quietest of our moodboards, with the type and imagery of another. The logo is Magalie, softened and customized. Gradients follow the sky from sunrise to sunset, one for each product, the change a body goes through on its way back.

A moodboard and a strategy deck. Audience validation with personas. The graphic path: logo, a palette in purple, blue and orange, Playfair Display with ITC Avant Garde Gothic, jar boxes, social templates, a tote, cards and the website hero. Brand guidelines. Packaging for capsules, electrolytes and loose-leaf tea, with labels and box dielines. Event pieces: a banner, a hat, a booth and business cards.

Fernando, at the graphic path presentation: "honestly, I'm impressed right now. I have a smile that I can't hold back." Later, in writing: "I decided to give you all full reins on the rebrand." On the tea packs: "The doypack for the teas look fantastic." His site now opens with the strategy line: "Your body isn't broken. It's backed up."

set.description:
Create was an AI app builder from San Francisco. You typed what you wanted and it came back as a working product, built with code. The company had been underestimated. Some early users had a bad experience, bigger rivals took the attention, and a launch date was already on the calendar. The brand had to be ready before it.

The brief put the whole problem in one sentence: "We're human in a space dominated by robotic AI branding." The team wanted to feel premium: powerful first, then beautiful, then intuitive, and free of the glow and gradients the category leans on. In the middle of the project they chose a new name for the product, Anything, and the identity had to carry it.

The first route had a symbol. The client saw a news network in it, so we dropped symbols altogether. The brand became typographic: an editorial serif italic set against a plain grotesk, so the wordmark itself shows an idea turning into a product. A second mark, overlapping shapes tilted upward, became the icon the team calls the rocket. Photography went soft and dreamlike, with a computer standing alone in a field.

The logo and symbol. A palette of light blue and deep navy with pink and cream. A type hierarchy, icons, photography directions, the homepage with its "i want to build a..." prompt, social templates, launch assets, and a brand book in PDF and Figma. Later, animations for the logo, the symbol and the icons.

Zaria Zinn, founding designer, the day after launch: "our launch was yesterday and it went very well!! Thank you all so so much for your help getting us ready for it! Also wanted to say the computer in a field image has been a huge hit! Everyone can't stop talking about it!" The funding round that followed made TechCrunch.

Our own identity. A lowercase serif wordmark in yellow and black, and a mark of a figure carrying the globe on its back, with a compass star and a globe as companions.

It lives on a water bottle, caps, a work jacket with enamel pins, a wax seal and posters. The posters carry the lines we work by, among them: "Built in Latin America, working across borders."

set.description:
Baristio is a coffee company built around the person behind the bar. Its app lets you choose your barista before you choose your drink, and the business planned to start on delivery apps, with a shop to follow. Emilio Orozco, a co-founder, came to us in 2025, before anything had launched. The contract put the goal in one line: a solid brand from day one.

Our first proposal read too masculine to Emilio. He wanted the brand to welcome women as much as men, and he pointed us to Good News Coffee in Barcelona. He also worried that a thin-line mark would break down in print and as an app icon. We reworked the direction after that meeting, and he approved it at the end of July.

The idea we wrote down was craft with people at the center: the barista promoted from server to maker, the customer from a sale to a relationship. The wordmark is custom, a condensed serif with sharp contrast, and a ©B monogram covers the small places, from the cup to the wax paper around a pastry. Brown and cream carry the system, with powder blue for contrast.

Brand strategy and the visual identity, icons and illustrations. Packaging for coffee and pastry: a sticker label, kraft and printed boxes, a can, a bag, gable pastry boxes, a waxed wrap and a handled bag, with a QR code on the bags and boxes. For the shop: cups, cards, a blade sign, an apron and a cap.

Emilio signed off the final pastry boxes in October 2025: "Everything looks good. Thanks!" By then the client's packaging lead had already chosen the printer he wanted to order from and asked us for the production files.

set.description:
Paola Díaz is a developmental specialist. She wanted to teach parents of babies and toddlers to read their child: on Instagram first, then through a free guide, then courses, then sessions one to one. She had no name, no logo and, by her own account, no founding story she believed in. Her challenge, in her words, was to stand out "in a fast, noisy, and trend-driven market" while staying calm inside it.

Content about early development swings between clinical advice nobody can apply at home and trendy posts that are easy to consume and leave nothing behind. Parents end up confused and tired. The opening was a calm, bilingual voice that puts connection first, for the earliest years of a child's life. Underneath it sits one belief: understanding comes before doing, and a regulated parent raises a regulated child.

We showed her Gentle Bloom, warm and drawn by hand, and Curious Guidance, with crayon strokes and vivid accents. Paola chose the first and asked to bring in the crayon marks from the second, with less orange and a softer logo. The ampersand in the name became the symbol, a parent holding a child. Fraunces brings the warmth and GT Walsheim the clarity. The photography shows parenting as it is, close and imperfect.

The name. A strategy deck with the belief, point of view, values, audience, positioning, messaging and tagline options. Brand guidelines with the wordmark, symbol, palette, type, illustrations for each stage of a baby's growth, the Instagram system, the newsletter and sets for recording. Website mockups. Then a copywriting system with content pillars, series and a launch calendar, and a run of Instagram carousels written to it.

At the presentation Paola said: "me encantó cómo explicas la marca, o sea, sí es más o menos todo lo que tenía en mente." The brand is live on Instagram and in her newsletter, set in Fraunces on soft linen.

set.description:
Bovi Health sells grass-fed beef colostrum and beef organ capsules. Its founders are Shannon Berg, a former college athlete, and Colson Myers, who has trained all his life, and their own line for the company is that health should be simple. They came to Atla at the end of 2024 with products made in the USA by a contract manufacturer and asked for the brand, the packaging and a site to sell from.

We showed them a rustic route with a community feel and another that mixed health science with luxury. Colson picked the rustic one and moved it east: rolling pastures, flowers, denim, red barns, embroidery, bottled milk and cows, "more 'east-coast farm' vibe as opposed to the more western vibe." Shannon fixed the words on the seal herself, Nature's Gold on top and Made in the USA below.

The wordmark is a cursive script drawn by hand, set in a roundel with a cow etched in a vintage line. The palette is soft: cream, sky blue, blush pink and a deep brown. Neutra Text and Nautica carry the type. The photography brief asks for love of the homeland and of the animals, and the pouches are shown in open pasture.

Vibe boards and moodboards, the logo and the brand guidelines, and labels for both products, taken through the manufacturer's compliance review. Then the website, which grew from a landing page into a full Shopify store with bundles and a page on why Bovi.

The manufacturer's quality lead wrote that the labels gave him "a farmhouse chic vibe that I think will do very well with consumers." At handover in May 2025, Shannon wrote: "It all looks great... We are very excited about how this turned out."

set.description:
Castro Capital invests in real estate development in San Luis Potosí. Its co-founders, Moisés and Sebastián Castro Martín del Campo, wanted the firm to be an ally to clients building commercial property, someone to help them make the best choices along the way. In 2021 they asked MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, for an identity to match that ambition.

The brief came down to a balance. The firm wanted to be seen as powerful and respected, and also as close and trustworthy. The monogram answers it by joining the C of Castro and the C of Capital with a plus sign, for what the firm adds to its projects and its investors. Around it, a modern and minimal system on a geometric grid, where the R and the P of the wordmark step forward.

Navy and royal blue carry the weight, with orange and cream for warmth, on a brand book, letterhead, email signatures, business cards and social templates. The posters speak to investors in plain Spanish: high-impact development, with transparent and concrete plans for where the money goes. The final files went out at the end of 2021.

Mindsparkle Mag published the work in March 2022. Through the following year, MK+2 sent it to prospective clients as a sample of its work.

set.description:
We built this identity for Conscious Care Co at MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, in early 2024. The design is made for kits of care at home: prompt cards for families, a candle, a book and a tote, sold from a site that invites you to explore the kits and nurture your home.

The system has a monogram, a primary logo and aligned versions, revised at the client's request to add a flower and a pair of hands. Dark green, brown and cream set the ground, with orange, light green, lavender and purple on top. VJ Category sets the titles and Mulish the text. The voice is direct: care about you.

set.description:
Huémac, from Querétaro, set out to be a platform for outdoor experiences: one place to book adventures with the best guides and companies, with safety and trust built in. Its audience ran from the young and adventurous to families and to travellers who wanted the softest version of the outdoors. In 2021 it came to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, for a strategy and an identity.

The strategy came first. The brand idea was "Con pasión, conexión", with adrenaline, trust and a wide range of activities as its flags. The mission was to make incredible experiences easy through a platform people can rely on. The vision went further: a platform that makes people fall in love with the planet and want to look after it.

The identity is warm and friendly. A yellow-orange serif wordmark sits on forest green, with coral and cream beside it, and a family of smiling mountains and hearts works as mascots on stickers and paper. The tone follows the personality written into the strategy: professional, adventurous, friendly and passionate.

A strategy deck, a moodboard, the graphic master and the identity presentation, then the final brand files at the end of 2021. Letterhead, envelopes, cards, stickers and a T-shirt for the guides, with the brand idea printed on the back.

set.description:
Mundã is a project of vacation and long-stay homes in La Saladita, on the coast of Guerrero, Mexico. Its full name is Mundã, Aldea del Mar, a village by the sea. The brand had to sell a way of living there, close to the waves and to the neighbors, on posters, on paper and on the wall at the entrance. We made it in 2022 at MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla.

The posters carry the line the brand was built on: strengthen your connection with nature, near the waves. Under it sat the values the client chose, connection with nature, fullness, community and a way of life. We kept the wordmark calm, a deep teal serif with a macron over the last A, and let the warmth come from drawings in thin orange line: palms, faces, people holding hands.

The logotype and its variants. Posters with the coastline coordinates, sunset photography and line illustrations. Envelopes, folders and business cards in deep teal, cream and burnt orange. Backlit signage for the entrance, shown in renders on a thatched gate. In 2023, animations of the mark and a looping beach scene.

In 2025 a prospective client wrote to us and named Mundã as the reference for her own brand. What she liked, in her words, was the simplicity of the brand, the people in it and its color palette, which she called interesting.

Oxylife is oxygenated water in a can, produced in Prague and imported into the United Arab Emirates. Suhail Alameri brought it to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, in 2021. He described it as the most stable oxygenated water in the world, sealed in a patented can coated on the inside. When we started, the brand still had no settled name.

The identity is a thin, wide serif wordmark on a white can, with black and a cool cyan. The label works in English and in Arabic. It carries the product's claim, unique oxygenated water, the line Power for your life, a heart drawn from the water and oxygen formulas, and small icons for when to drink it: driving, flying, at the gym, at work.

A branding presentation, the logo and the can label. MK+2 used the work as one of its sales cases through the following year, and the water is still produced in Prague today.

Pathize Health builds an app for people who live with energy-limiting conditions such as Long COVID, ME/CFS and POTS. It reads data from wearables like Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin and Polar, and helps each person pace the day against a personal limit. In 2023 the team came to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, on a referral from the founder of Peachy, with a website relaunch close behind.

Alex Bahram wrote the brief. He wanted a mix of serif and sans serif, a strong name and a strong logo that did not clash, colors that felt soft and welcoming without leaning feminine, and illustration alongside lifestyle photography. The team chose the first moodboard and then the first logo, and Lex Oiler wrote back: "We really love the logotype (simple! clean!) and love the heart."

The heart is the icon. It is made of pills that meet, and the break between the lines is what makes it read. Lex noticed it would animate well out of the P of Pathize. Cooper Light sets the titles and Circular the text, on cream, sky blue, mint and mustard. Hand-drawn illustrations and scribbles mark the words that matter, the way a person marks up a document.

Moodboards, the logo, a palette, illustrations and scribbles, a brand book, and applications: business cards, letterhead, the app icon, a pacing screen and pages for the website. The team asked for the raw files and the brand book in a hurry, to finish the relaunch. When it was done, Lex wrote: "We loved working with you guys."

set.description:
Pax & Beneficia opened in Las Colinas in 2019 and grew across Dallas-Fort Worth, roasting its own beans. The name means peace and blessings, and the cafés are built on it: a guest is an honored visitor. The company sells roasted coffee and handcrafted syrups online as well as over the counter. A brand existed, and it had fallen behind the mission.

In our reading, specialty coffee is crowded and much of it looks alike. The challenge was an identity bold enough to stand out on a shelf and still true to the café culture that started the company, carried from Turkey and Andalusia to Texas. It also had to work as a system, because new locations kept opening.

The mark is a tree: deep roots, growth outward. Apercu Mono sets the type, in warm earth tones with brighter accents. The company lives by its values, each a pair of P and B words: Prosper & Bond, Persevere & Become, Pause & Breathe, Patience & Belief, Pursue & Beckon. We turned each one into a linocut illustration, so the values travel on the bag instead of staying in a document.

The logo and its animation, an icon, iconography, a pattern and the type system. Packaging: the coffee bag, a box, labels and labels for the syrup bottles. The value illustrations, then applied across cups, totes, cans and shop windows.

set.description:
Peachy is a healthcare startup built for patients, founded by Lex Oiler, a designer who became a founder. In 2022 the team came to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, after trying to brand the company themselves. Lex put the problem in one sentence: "I had no idea branding for my startup would end up being the hardest part of my job."

The wordmark is a heavy serif, customized so every letter fits its neighbors while keeping its own bars and curves. To balance that weight, the icon is a smiling heart with a leaf on top, light and friendly, a little like a hairstyle. The team chose the bolder version of the logotype. Stickers carry the voice: for patients by patients, healthcare made easy, along for the ride with you.

The branding presentation, the logotype and the icon, a palette of peach, red, pink, light blue, yellow and cream, a set of stickers, and applications from posters and banners to envelopes and cards. The elements and assets went out in June 2022. That summer we also designed a quick-pay screen for the product, so patients could pay their providers faster.

Lex's verdict, written for us to share: "My only regret was not finding José and his team sooner. I'd recommend them to any of my friends." The following year he sent us Pathize Health.

PuppyPy makes silicone holders that clip a tracking tag onto a dog's collar. In 2022 its founder, Gilad Rom, was renaming and rebuilding the company, then called Huan, to come back to market with a product that had already proved itself. MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, took it on that spring, as the studio was starting to work with clients in the United States.

We started with the name. Gilad picked Puppy Py, after his own dog, Puppy Pie, whose spelling was already taken, and asked us: "If you can find a creative way around that it would be amazing!" The answer runs the name together in lowercase, stacked as pu ppy py, with a pPy monogram for the small places.

Color, illustration and photography carry the rest: bright yellow, red, orange, pink and lime, a dachshund wearing a rainbow holder, and a line that sums up the product, stand out from the pack. The moodboard, the branding presentation and the final files went out in June 2022. Gilad then redesigned the website himself on top of them.

He also introduced us to a friend who, in Gilad's words, "was very impressed with the work you did for me!"

set.description:
Reggie makes calming chews, supplements and feeder mats for dogs. The name is short for regimen. New owners from New Zealand bought the company in 2025 and inherited the original brand, a refresh from the year before, and the watered-down version the old team had actually shipped, white jars and all. They wanted to rebuild while flying, moving from direct sales into retail, with a trade show on the calendar.

Simon Doig, co-owner, wrote the problem down: "if we are going to make the change again, we really want to get it right, and produce something special." The refresh looked cleaner and might not stand out on a shelf. The brief ruled out anything overbearing or clinical. The tone had to be the friend who does not judge, and the supplements had to feel like treats.

The idea in our insight work was trust as an emotion: a brand that feels like a relationship, with routine as ritual and science said in a human voice. With the partner studio Vapor and the owners' direction, we brought the logo out stronger, anchored on the brand green, dropped the brown, and gave the mascot fill, shading and bolder lines, so Reggie the dog became an asset again.

Discovery and insight decks comparing the brands in market. A brand identity and its digital expression: wordmark, logo, type, palettes, photography direction and avatar. Website design for the homepage, collection, product, cart and checkout, about, blog, email, pop-ups and a design system. Packaging and labels for the focus products: jars, a pouch, a dropper and the feeder-mat pack.

Ricardo Camargo, of Vapor Studio, when the site went live: "Reggie.com is live and it looks great. Congratulations to the team, great work." The brand was relaunched at SuperZoo in Las Vegas that August.

set.description:
Sexto Abismo is a gin from San Luis Potosí. The name comes from the Sótano de las Golondrinas in the Huasteca Potosina, one of the deepest abysses on earth. José Pablo started the brand in 2021 with Oscar Gómez and Rodrigo Espinosa, and built its identity at MK+2, his studio before Atla. There was no outside client and no brief, only a bottle to fill and a region to put on the label.

Most gin borrows its look from Britain. Mexico has its own mystique, and Mexican surrealism offered more material than one label could hold. The hard part was choosing. The story on the bottle had to matter as much as the liquid inside it.

The icon is a swallow taking flight from an abyss under an eclipse, a sign of passage from one state to another. The wordmark is a custom organic letterform whose letters change size as they go. The label tells a story: a stranger crosses an abyss, meets La Felina and El Lacayo, drinks something clear and wakes in another world, where the characters watch him.

The name and the story. A brand book, the bottle label and the shipping box. Posters, stickers, postcards, a menu, a billboard, a mural, tent cards for the house cocktails, a trailer and a book for bartenders. In 2025, Atla added a content strategy and a refresh deck for the brand.

The gin went on sale in Mexico in 2022. In 2024 the Beverage Testing Institute gave it a Silver Medal and rated it Highly Recommended.

set.description:
Shop Latinx is a marketplace for Latino brands in beauty, fashion and lifestyle, founded by Brittany Chavez to give those brands visibility in the North American market. It started as a fashion brand and, as we wrote at the time, it lacked the folklore of the culture it served. In 2022 Brittany brought it to MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, to rebrand it without falling into stereotypes.

The new identity is Y2K: a chrome wordmark on a pink ellipse over a blue and green gradient, airbrushed hibiscus, and an SLX monogram that works as a pill, a necklace and a gold hoop earring. The posters talk to the community directly, with lines like "Seen, supported, and celebrated" and "Guided from above, grounded from below."

María Martínez led the design. The brief, the branding presentation and the reviews ran through July 2022, and then weekly work on social graphics and the Shopify store until the end of the year. The posters describe the marketplace in Brittany's own terms: by us, for us.

That September, Brittany introduced us to Frank Bach, who was "extremely impressed with SLX's new branding", and described MK+2 to contacts at a16z as "the 360 agency that I've been working with."

set.description:
Carlos Alvarado built Tequila Unido alone. Born in Eagle Pass, Texas, with grandparents from Guadalajara and a father who sang mariachi, he calls himself "tejano jalisciense." He registered the name, partnered with a family distillery in Arandas founded in 1915, carried samples by bus to Dallas distributors, and came to us with a symbol, a bottle and a blue label. The brand had to be clarified and kept.

Look at a tequila shelf and the blue is everywhere. His symbol, a rigid geometric knot in a circle, read like a keyboard key. And Carlos set conditions. His culture could never become a costume, and the story could not be about him: "hay que hacer mi historia en la historia de todos." Unido had to mean something you could say at a bar.

The idea was already in his brief: "unido is how you order it." Good tequila is offered and shared. We took the mariachi, his father's trade, as the cultural key without naming the family: a medallion label shaped by the sombrero, ornaments from the brooches of a mariachi jacket, a symbol that reads as rope, ribbon or bow. Paper, deep red, gold and green. The eagle was redrawn: the first one, in his words, was a pigeon.

A moodboard and the brand direction. Labels for Blanco, Reposado, Añejo and Extra Añejo, and the small bottle. Brand guidelines with the custom wordmark, symbol, badges, Schoolbook and Latino Gothic, photography direction and the Instagram system. A coming-soon page. The case box and the shipper art, ready to print for the distributor.

Carlos, on the first presentation: "sí me gusta mucho el concepto del sombrero del mariachi con el logo, siento que sí me entendieron." On the final white Blanco label: "I love it. I think that's the one." And: "I feel extremely blessed and happy to have you guys on board."

The Branding Academy is José Pablo's weekly newsletter for founders and the people who run brands. It was named at the end of 2025 and runs on Substack. It began as a reply on Instagram: comment academy, and he sends you a branding strategy every week. The identity treats the newsletter as a school: a seal, and a row of bound books in pastel cloth.

The mark is a round seal that stacks the letters A, T and B into one monogram, stamped in gold on cloth book spines of blue, coral, mustard and mint. Line drawings of hands at work carry the illustration. On the phone, the newsletter opens with the idea behind it: branding is a structural decision before it becomes a visual one.

Seal and wordmark, palette, illustration, the newsletter layout, and things to carry it: notebooks, a tote, a cap and cards. Readers sign up through Substack. Sponsors have written asking to advertise in it, and in November 2026 another studio shared it with its own community.

set.description:
TigreTigre is a sushi and sake restaurant on Avenida Chapultepec in San Luis Potosí, opened by José Pablo and his partners in 2023. The pitch fits on a sticker: after-office sake and food. Japanese comfort plates made with good ingredients, cocktails and premium sake, a place to land when the day ends. The brand was made at MK+2, his studio before Atla, before the doors opened.

The restaurant is casual on a Tuesday, with ramen and sake, and formal on a Saturday, with author plates, and it needed a brand that could be both. The name already repeats itself. The identity had to turn that repetition into a character, so the place would read as one restaurant across both moods.

The wordmark mixes a casual type style with a formal one, so the name moves. The icon is a double-headed tiger sharing one eye, the duality and the repetition taken straight from the name. A kanji mark, 虎虎, covers the small places. Stickers carry the voice for everything else, with lines like "Sake it off" and "Have a rice day."

The logotype and its variants, the double-headed tiger, the kanji mark, color and type. Stationery and cards, stickers and labels, the menu, posters and flyers, a bag and packaging mockup, social templates and the design of the first website.

The restaurant is open, with a new menu for 2026.

Torre Avancer is an office tower on Avenida Chapultepec in San Luis Potosí, one of the holdings of Grupo Avancer, a company with businesses in flavors and fragrances, finance, real estate and hotels. The building came before the brand. Its irregular geometry was drawn to recall the semi-desert around the city, and the tower had already won awards when the owners asked us for its identity.

The hard part, as we wrote in our notes at the time, was working inside identities that already existed, starting with the architecture itself. So the logotype is purely typographic, set in capitals, TORRE in a light weight and AVANCER in bold. The icon is a set of vertical lines taken from the architect's own sketches of the tower. The aim was a brand quiet enough to point at the building's details without covering them.

The logotype and the icon. A signage system drawn for the building: the entrance totem, the lobby directory with its restaurant and bar, pictograms, and a logo plate cut from metal. Stationery, folders and posters in dusty pink, terracotta and rust, with the sketch of the tower printed in ink. Social media for the tower and its tenants from 2021 to 2023.

We made it in 2022 at MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, working with Elipsis Arquitectos. Signage was a service the studio had never offered before. It started with this building, drawn so the signs would read as part of the structure rather than additions to it.

Stationery, folders and posters in dusty pink, terracotta and rust, with the sketch of the tower printed in ink. Social media for the tower and its tenants from 2021 to 2023.

We made it in 2022 at MK+2, José Pablo's studio before Atla, working with Elipsis Arquitectos. Signage was a service the studio had never offered before. It started with this building, drawn so the signs would read as part of the structure rather than additions to it.

WeLoveDaily is the design curation network José Pablo runs beside Atla. It shares other studios' work in branding, illustration, animation, web and AI design, from accounts that post under the WeLove name. In 2026 it added a publication of its own at welovedaily.net, built blog first, and the identity had to hold a magazine as well as a feed.

The brand book sets one lowercase wordmark, welove, in a rounded sans, and gives each section of the publication its own color: Branding, Illustration, Animation, Web Design and AI Design. Cobalt blue carries the rest, with black, cream and white. Type, photography, social templates, the website and the favicon all come from the same book.
